 Judgment

This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed by the appellant, challenging the order dated 26.04.2016 passed in M.C.O.P.No.1573 of 2011 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal / learned Principal District Judge, Tiruchirappalli.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal / learned Principal District Judge, Tiruchirappalli
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2.The victim, namely, Pushpavalli, initially filed a claim petition, seeking compensation for the injuries suffered by her, stating that while she was walking on a public road, a two wheeler insured with the appellant bearing Registration No.TN 48 P 8259 came in a rash and negligent manner and collided with the 1st claimant and caused grievous injuries, including fracture and dislocation of the hip, fracture of the rib bones and grievous injuries on the head; that four months after the accident,
the victim died on 22.08.2011 and therefore, the respondents 1 to 3 herein filed an impleading petition and sought compensation for the death of the original claimant.
3.The owner of the two wheeler / 4th respondent herein remained ex-parte before the tribunal.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

4.The appellant filed counter affidavit, stating that the accident occurred only due to the negligence of the deceased, who crossed the road in a negligent manner; and that therefore, they are not liable to pay any compensation.
5.The respondents 1 to 3 examined three witnesses on their side and marked Ex.P.1 to P.7.
The medical report of the deceased was marked as Ex.X1.
The appellant neither examined any witnesses nor marked any documents.

6.The Tribunal, after taking into consideration oral and documentary evidence, held that there was a nexus between the death of the deceased and the accident and determined the compensation at Rs.4,82,000/- (Rupees Four Lakhs and Eighty Two Thousand Only), payable by the appellant.

7.The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the respondents 1 to 3 had not established the nexus between the accident and the death, which took place four months later and further, they had neither marked postmortem certificate nor produced the details of the treatment taken by the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis deceased during the four months period to establish the nexus;
and that in any event, from the nature of the injury, the nexus cannot be inferred.
8.The learned counsel further submitted that even assuming that the nexus has been established,
the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, is excessive and prayed for reduction of the compensation.
9.The learned counsel for the respondents 1 to 3, per contra, has submitted that the injured was 55 years old at the time of the accident and was hale and healthy and because of the grievous injuries,
such as a hip fracture, she was bedridden, which resulted in her death; that the mere fact that no postmortem certificate was produced, cannot be put against the claimants, as the facts reveal that M/S.United India Insurance Co. (i) Abdul Rahim and another Vs. Sundaresan and another reported in 2010 (1) TN MAC 205 and (ii) United India Insurance Company Ltd., and Sivagami and others reported in 2010 (1) L.W.614.
10.This

11.The

points for consideration in the instant appeal are as follows:-
A. Whether the respondents 1 to 3 had established the nexus between the accident and the death of the victim and the Tribunal was right in awarding compensation for the death of the victim?; and B. Whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable ?.
12.As regards the first issue, it is seen from Ex.X1 that the victim was 55 years old at the time of the accident and had sustained serious injuries, including hip fracture and other grievous injuries.
The details of the treatment taken by the deceased are found in Ex.X1, which was marked by the consent of both parties before the Tribunal.

The claimants had marked Ex.P.7 certificate issued by the Doctor, which enumerates the injuries suffered by the deceased, including hip fractures and lung injuries and the treatment taken till 21.04.2011.
PW.3 Doctor examined on the side of the claimants had also stated about the certificate issued by him and the treatment given to the victim.
There is no other evidence on record to show that the deceased suffered from a pre-existing disease.

Though it is a fact that the claimants had not produced the postmortem certificate and had not proved the exact cause of the death, considering the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis nature of the injuries suffered by the deceased, her age and the proximity in time of the accident and the death
, this Court can infer that there is a nexus between the injury and the death.
13.In similar circumstances, this Court, in the judgment cited supra referred to by the learned counsel for the respondents, had inferred such a nexus.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that the award of the Tribunal, granting compensation for the death of the deceased, is in accordance with the law and therefore, it deserves to be confirmed.
The first point is answered accordingly.
14.As regards the second point, the claimants had deposed before the Tribunal that the deceased was working as Coolie.
However, no other evidence has been provided to substantiate the said fact.
The deceased was aged about 55 years and in the absence of any evidence either to prove avocation or income, the Tribunal was justified in fixing the notional income.
15.In the facts and circumstances, this Court is of the view that it would be just and reasonable to fix the notional income as Rs.5,000/- instead of Rs.6,000/- as fixed by the Tribunal.
Further, since there were three dependants, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 1/3rd is to be deducted towards personal expenses and the multiplier applicable is 9.

Hence, the monthly income, after adding 10%
towards future prospects, comes to Rs.5,500/-.

Therefore, the amount under the head of loss of M/S.United India Insurance Co. Ltd vs Pushpavalli (Died) on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38274523/

Rs.5,500 x 12 x 9 x 2/3 = Rs.3,96,000/-.

Reduc  Loss of Love and Rs.30,000 Rs.30,000/- Confi  Affection  Transport Expenses Rs.10,000/- Rs.10,000/- Confi  Funeral Expenses Rs.10,000/- Rs.10,000/- Confi  Total Compensation Rs.4,82,000/- Rs.4,46,000/- By re  a sum  Rs./-
17.The

appellant Insurance Company is directed to deposit the award amount modified by this Court together with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization (excluding https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the period of dismissal for default if any)
and costs, less the amount already deposited, if any,
within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

18.On such a deposit, the respondents 1 to 3 are permitted to withdraw the same as per the apportionment fixed by the Tribunal, less the amount, if any, already withdrawn, by filing an appropriate application before the Tribunal.
19.In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed.
No costs.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is also closed.
